clue.text: Female faking sex now, organ not to be trusted?

indicators.note: faking means falsifying, so the letters of the words sex now are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman pretending in bed, and a remark about an untrustworthy body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks anatomical after the sexual surface, but it means a mouthpiece or media outlet; the question mark flags the jibe at an American broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ can mean a medium of news or opinion; this US channel is often accused of partisan, unreliable reporting.

clue.text: Lift prince by the ears?

indicators.note: taken in by the ears, the word is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: Prince Philip, the late Duke of Edinburgh, so the name Philip

explanation.surface: Hoisting a royal up by his ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or stimulus to spirits is a lift; the answer is a synonym for that noun.

clue.text: Relations with 12 looking up for old 12

definitions.note: an ancient ruler: a Persian monarch of the fifth century BC

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the pieces from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: sexual relations, so sex
12 across is a monarch; rex is Latin for a king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: Family members joining a monarch take a turn for the better, on behalf of a former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue cross-refers to 12 across twice, once for the Latin letters inside and once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great ruled the Persian Empire, so he is an ancient monarch.

clue.text: Previous individual assessed, found not guilty

parts.note: ex means former or previous
one means a single individual
rated means evaluated or assessed

explanation.surface: A defendant's past record is weighed up and they are acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cleared of blame or acquitted is to be found not guilty in court.

clue.text: Originally starring George Osborne, say, one employed to change film script

definitions.text: one employed to change film script

indicators.note: originally means taking the opening letter of the word starring

parts.note: the former Conservative Chancellor became ... of the Evening Standard newspaper, so a Tory ...

explanation.surface: A former Chancellor is cast in a movie, and someone is hired to rewrite it.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne, the Conservative (Tory) Chancellor of the Exchequer, became editor of London's Evening Standard in 2017, which supplies the last nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In film and television, this role develops and revises screenplays, so it is a job of altering scripts.

clue.text: Chops primarily one's splitting, as tool

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of the word chops

parts.note: one who is splitting, i.e. departing, is a leaver

explanation.surface: A butcher chops, chiefly with a blade that splits meat, used as a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy chopping knife used by butchers is a cutting implement, so a tool.

clue.text: Round middle of tree, apple was also highly featured

indicators.note: round means going around, so the apple variety encloses the central letters

parts.note: a costard is an old English variety of cooking apple

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters of the word tree

explanation.surface: An apple sitting about the middle of a tree was given a starring role too.
explanation.walkthrough: The costard, a large English cooking apple, is not widely known; it gives the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To have shared top billing with another performer is to have been prominently featured as well.

clue.text: Lake near river, oddly drained

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of the words near river are drained away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A lake close to a river has dried up strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America, between Ontario and Ohio.

clue.text: World leader — negotiating with Trump and I invalid

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working something around, so the letters of Trump, I and invalid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A world leader is in talks with the US president, while the speaker is incapacitated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' is only a link; the fodder is TRUMP, I and INVALID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian president has been one of the most powerful heads of state on the global stage.

clue.text: Funny parts author, scratching head, gets to attach again

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the joke goes into the middle of the shortened surname
scratching head means the first letter of the surname is struck out

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist
a funny is a joke, i.e. a gag

explanation.surface: A writer of comic passages, scratching his head, gets around to fastening things again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' reads as an adjective but is a noun, a joke; it 'parts' the shortened author.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage a gear or mechanism once more is to connect or attach it again.

clue.text: Broadly similar, gold cups

indicators.note: cups means holds within, so the letters sit inside the words similar, gold

explanation.surface: Two gold trophies that are much alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadly similar' reads as one phrase, but 'Broadly' alone is the definition, a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, this Italian tempo marking directs playing slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Stubborn stain needs to be shifted

indicators.note: shifted means moved around, so the letters of stain and to be are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn stain must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is only a link; 'stubborn stain' is a stock phrase hiding the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinate refuses to change their mind, a direct synonym for stubborn.

clue.text: Completely fashionable, sewn?

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
the letters S, E, W, N are the four compass points, so they point in all directions

explanation.surface: A garment that is wholly trendy, stitched together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewn' is not about stitching: its letters are South, East, West and North.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in all respects, entirely, so totally or completely.

clue.text: Top guy, Ali departs African capital having shut up Foreman, finally

indicators.note: shut up means enclosed, so the shortened city holds the next letter
departs means the name Ali leaves the capital city's name

parts.note: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word Foreman

explanation.surface: Muhammad Ali leaves an African capital having silenced George Foreman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Rumble in the Jungle, when Ali beat Foreman in Kinshasa, but the capital needed is Kigali.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the person at the top of a realm, so a top guy.

clue.text: Sorcerer's inspired upon newly embracing Mahler's first great work

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the sorcerer takes the following letters inside

parts.note: a magus is a sorcerer or wise man; the 's is read as 'is', a link

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the rearranged letters enclose the initial
newly means made afresh, so the letters of upon are rearranged
first takes the opening letter of the word Mahler's

explanation.surface: A wizard is inspired by Mahler's First Symphony, now taken to heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names an artist's masterpiece, their greatest or most important work.

clue.text: Liberal Democrats initially anger PM, a sin taking more than one seat?

indicators.note: liberal means free, loosely treated, so the letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of the word Democrats

explanation.surface: A political party annoys the Prime Minister, whose offence is holding several parliamentary seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Democrats' reads as the UK party, but 'Liberal' is the anagram signal and only D is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The habit of a man sitting with legs wide apart on public transport occupies extra seats; the question mark flags the political pun.

clue.text: In season, blossoming?

indicators.note: In means the word for blossoming is set inside the season

parts.note: spring is a season of the year
flowers that are blossoming are out

explanation.surface: Plants coming into flower at the right time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: flowers out in spring are budding.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting out shoots or buds is how plants begin to blossom in spring.

clue.text: Dogged attitude defining leaders in broadcast

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed within the broadcast word

parts.note: broadcast means shown, so showed

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the words attitude and defining

explanation.surface: A determined stance shapes the headlines on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like an adjective, determined, but is the verb: followed closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, which is to tail or track them.

clue.text: Nose picking beginning to obsess cheeky character

indicators.note: picking means taking up, so the snooping word gathers the next letters inside it

parts.note: to nose is to pry, to snoop

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word obsess

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: A cheeky person starts to fixate on picking their nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic quality or attribute of something, its character, is one of its properties.

clue.text: Hard or firm, call commercial breaks shrewd business

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
set means firm or solid, as of jelly

indicators.note: breaks means splits into, so the commercial goes into the call

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Hard business news: a firm's call during the advert break.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-headed bargaining or shrewd deal-making, originally the sharp dealing of horse dealers.

clue.text: See 4
Look good with weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: An instruction to admire an attractive weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look or quick peek at something, a synonym for look as a noun.

clue.text: Trick unionists' alliance, ultimately

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word alliance

explanation.surface: A con involving the Unionists' alliance in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP, Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, was propping up the UK government when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to deceive or trick them.

clue.text: Moss perhaps old, presume going to seed?

indicators.note: going to seed means deteriorating, so the letters of old and presume are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moss, possibly getting old, gone to seed in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moss' looks like a plant beside 'going to seed', but it is Kate Moss, the British fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is an example of a top international fashion model.

clue.text: The heavens opening in earnest, the rainstorm's beginning

indicators.note: opening in suggests a gap made inside the two initials, where the word the is placed
beginning takes the first letters of the words earnest and rainstorm's

explanation.surface: The skies open in earnest as a downpour starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'the' sits between the initials of 'earnest' and 'rainstorm's'. 'The heavens opening' suggests rain, but only 'The heavens' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the ether is the clear upper sky, the heavens above.

clue.text: Order to be civil, it having restricted youth?

parts.note: as in 'as it had rained', the word as means it having been the case

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a boy is a youth

explanation.surface: A court order demanding good manners, having curbed a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a civil court order against nuisance behaviour, often imposed on teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: This British court order required its subject to stop antisocial acts, in effect to behave civilly.

clue.text: Gold medal alongside pens for prolific writer

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the alongside word holds the gold and medal

parts.note: with means alongside or accompanying
or is gold in heraldry
DSM is the Distinguished Service Medal

explanation.surface: An author with a gold medal pens yet another book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing beside 'writer', but it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled and productive user of words, so a writer who turns out a lot.

clue.text: See 7
Always pound squeezed by foreign currency for a short period

indicators.note: squeezed by means pressed inside, so the currency holds the other letters

parts.note: the dong is the currency of Vietnam
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Sterling is perpetually pinched by a foreign currency for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wry: lasting a single day is only a short period.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting the length of one day, which is a brief span of time.

clue.text: Book store

definitions.meaning: to book is to make a booking in advance
a store is a supply kept back for later use

explanation.surface: Reserving a book in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to book ahead a table or seat; the other is a stock kept back, a store.
